newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's FIS condemns attacks, backs peace move.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's FIS condemns attacks, backs peace move.

text.p: Algeria's outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) condemned on Tuesday the current upsurge of violence in the strife-torn North African country and backed an appeal to mobilise for peace.
In a statement from its leadership-in-exile received in Paris, FIS called the recent escalation in bloody attacks "unbelievable" and "mind-boggling".

"We call upon all those who adore their religion and homeland to categorically denounce these crimes not only because they are contrary to the teachings and spirit of Islam but because they are an insult to humanitarian feelings," it said.

At least 40 people have been killed and 150 wounded in bomb attacks in the past month, almost exactly from the day Algerian President Liamine Zeroual announced that a referendum to change the constitution would be held on November 28.
A further 78 people, including women and children, have been slaughtered, most by having their throats cut, in three operations in the same period blamed on fundamentalist rebels.
"FIS strongly denounces criminal acts against children, women and elderly people," the statement said.
More than 50,000 people are estimated to have been killed since violence erupted in 1992 after the authorities cancelled a general election dominated by FIS.
FIS has put the death toll at 120,000.
It said the referendum, which proposes to ban parties based on religion, would "confiscate the sovereignty of the Algerian people...and legalise the dictatorship of the president".
The FIS statement voiced support for a statement published at the weekend by prominent Algerians which called for Algerians to mobilise for peace.

The statement, whose signatories included former president Ahmed Ben Bella, former ministers and others, spoke of "tens of thousands of dead, mutilated, widowed, orphaned, and political detainees, victims of the cycle of violence and repression".

"We globally encourage the appeal for peace launched recently by a group of national personalities and we reiterate our support for any action that would allow the Algerian people to recover peace, security, freedom and sovereignty," FIS added.
